title: The Missing Moon: an AI-authored two-player mystery — looking for four pairs to test the deductions
author: Flashy-Tiger6015
selftext:
I'm exploring a small website selling two-person detective cases. This free prototype was built with AI agents in Codex: they drafted the puzzle design, evidence text and React interface. No human playtest has happened yet, and a proposed longer $12 case is not available to buy.

The experiment is whether a short, text-led mystery gives both players useful work. Each player sees a different evidence file on their own device. They have to talk through two linked deductions, with optional hints and a final explanation. Allow roughly ten minutes, although that estimate has not been tested.

The most useful part of the development process was turning the puzzle assumptions into an explicit check. A separate script reconstructs the evidence and verifies a unique feasible suspect. It also checks that skipping either deduction leaves ambiguity, so the earlier puzzle matters to the conclusion. The game uses a fixed solution; it does not generate answers during play.

The unresolved part is whether this feels satisfying to people. An agent can verify the intended logic while missing awkward wording, unequal participation or a puzzle that feels like a worksheet. The build and TypeScript checks passed and the public start page opens, but a complete browser playthrough and mobile visual check are still outstanding. Human feedback could overturn the design.

[Play The Missing Moon](https://two-sided-casefiles-sample.abuzz-wasp-5495.chatgpt.site)

I'd appreciate four pairs trying it and replying with their completion time, hint use, whether both partners contributed, any confusion or device problems, and an enjoyment score from 1–5. Would you choose another case in this style over something you have already played? Negative feedback is useful; there is no payment or request for a positive review.

Open the link on two devices and choose different roles. Each person submits answers on their own screen. Reloading resets progress, and the page collects no answers or feedback. Please put solution details behind spoiler tags and leave out personal information.

For other developers, what would you check when evaluating an AI-authored cooperative puzzle beyond whether its solution is logically unique?
